text:
alexa_fincorp: Hi — we're seeing a sudden increase in 429 responses from your inference endpoint starting ~11:57 PT. ~15% of requests return 429 even though our overall qps hasn't changed much. We're on the "scale-small" plan, client_id=acme-frontend. Can someone take a look?

sara_support: Sorry for the trouble — can you paste a sample request id or the raw response headers? Also which region/endpoint? @james_sre fyi.

alexa_fincorp: sample request id: req_0a1b2c3d; region: us-west-2. Here's a sanitized curl:
```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \
  -H "X-Client-Id: acme-frontend" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-xyz","input":"hi"}'
```
Response headers they sent back:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-limit: 1200
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 45
x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d
```

mike_dev: Thanks — that looks like you exhausted a per-minute quota (short-window). Are you going through an aggregator/gateway that might fan out? Any client retries configured?

alexa_fincorp: We have a server-side retry loop: 3 fast retries with 200ms backoff on 5xx and 429. No client-side global token bucket or batching.

james_sre: @sara_support I'm pulling metrics now. Alexa — can you share traffic shape for the last 15m (1s or 5s series is ideal)? We want to check short-window RPM spikes, not just average.

alexa_fincorp: quick paste of 1m samples: 11:45 18 rps, 11:46 18, 11:47 22, 11:48 19, 11:49 35, 11:50 19, 11:51 20, 11:52 24, 11:53 60, 11:54 20 — there was a short burst at :53 from a backend batch job that hit many endpoints at once.

ops-bot: alert: quota-exhaustion detected for customer acme-frontend in us-west-2 — 1m rolling avg = 1175 rpm, configured limit = 1200 rpm, observed short-window peak = 1800 rpm at 11:53.

sara_support: That matches — short-window burst exceeded the per-minute cap, so some requests were rejected while the aggregate rate recovered. Two immediate recommendations: 
1) Client-side: implement exponential backoff with jitter and cap retries on 429 (avoid tight retry loops).
2) Infra: consider a small burst allowance or a proxy that batches/queues requests to smooth bursts. We can open an emergency burst override if needed.

mike_dev: Also verify token-level usage: if a few requests contain long prompts you could hit token-per-minute (TPM) limits even at modest request rates. Can you share typical prompt/token sizes?

alexa_fincorp: Most calls are ~60 tokens. The batch job sent ~10k requests in ~60s — looks like the fanout caused the short spike. We'll throttle that batch. Quick question: do you return a canonical header we should respect for retry timing?

james_sre: We return `Retry-After` when applicable and `x-rate-limit-reset` (seconds until window reset). Use those headers if present. For longer-term, switch retries to exponential with jitter and add a client-side token bucket. I'm pushing a one-time short burst allowance for today to avoid an outage — @sara_support can you trigger approvals?

sara_support: Opening emergency ops ticket SUP-4123 to approve a 2-minute burst allowance and notify billing. Meanwhile recommend adding a 2-per-second client limiter on the batch job.

alexa_fincorp: Thanks — we'll deploy the limiter within 15m and disable the aggressive retries. Appreciate the quick help :pray:

sara_support: SUP-4123 created, ops + billing looped in. Reach out here if you see anything after the client fix. :thumbsup:
